Judged by tests/host/fuel-gauge-check.sh against battery-ok.sh's fastboot reading, within 100 mV.
why: Only the binding, driver and node are needed for walleye; z21's init already has the command loop that reads power_supply. One change per try.
rejected: Taking all eight patches: five are other boards' dts. Porting the vendor battery profile into a table of ours: the driver does not load one. Changing the init for the try: a second change in one image.

brief: No kernel module and no reset_controller to read UFS_HW_VERSION: the matched UFS image reads it (0xE4) in its own probe and picks the PHY table by it
decision: UFS_HW_VERSION (register 0xE4) and the PHY registers are not read on live Android. The matched image (item walleye-ufs-match-android-z) reads 0xE4 in its own ufs-qcom init, where the vendor driver reads it (clocks on, PHY not yet initialised), prints it, and selects the PHY rate-A table by it (3.0.0 or 3.1.0, as the vendor does; any other value: no PHY init and a stop, as the vendor's -ENODEV).
why: The vendor driver accepts only 3.0.0 and 3.1.0 and live Android's UFS works, so the version is one of two for certain; debugfs reaches only 0x00-0x9c, and the one debugfs path that dumps the vendor block (reset_controller) resets the host: not read-only. A module is a day of build against the unread Lineage 4.4.302 tree for one word, with a bus-hang risk on a clock-gated host. The author's wait holds the UFS probe anyway.
rejected: Read-only kernel module on live Android (cost and a bus-hang restart for one word; kept as a fallback only if a read before the try is asked for); debugfs reset_controller (writes, resets the disk's host); vendor kernel as instrument (same /dev/mem gap, host unclocked); guessing the table from mainline's equal-to-3.1.0 lines (not a reading)

brief: The matched UFS image may be built and reviewed before the author's go; it is never booted without it (gate refuses it)
decision: walleye-ufs-match-android-z is built now: a UFS-on image that is built, reviewed by the programmer and left in the build tree under a name that says ufs-on, never booted, never put in a keeper's queue. The try keeps waiting for the author's explicit go (decision 2026-11-18-walleye-ufs-wait); the gate tests/host/ufs-off-image.sh refuses any UFS-on image before a boot, and nothing here weakens it.
why: z13 was built and left unrun on the same wait, the author's 'Yes, wait' is about the UFS probe from our kernel on the phone, not about building; the build touches no phone. Wifi, audio, radios and the display chain all wait on UFS, so a reviewed image makes the author's later go a plain yes or no on a finished thing, and the one lane that can move unattended is this build. Research walleye-ufs-regs-reader-verdict removed the last block (the register read moves into the image's own probe).
rejected: Wait to build until the go (idles the only unattended piece and makes the go a decision about an image not yet seen); building a UFS-off variant (proves nothing about the UFS path); weakening or skipping the gate to try on a fallback (never: no EDL way back, decision 2026-11-18-walleye-edl-no-way-back-wait-holds)

brief: The UFS hold has a second way out: Android's UFS bring-up of this card understood 'atmost sure' (author's words); the final go stays his
decision: The hold of decision 2026-11-18-walleye-ufs-wait ends in two ways, not one: (a) an EDL way back for walleye is known, or (b) we understand how Android brings up this exact card's UFS well enough to be 'atmost sure' - the matched image (walleye-ufs-match-android-z) is the work heading there. In either case the author says the go himself, in his own words; no session lifts the hold by its own judgement. When the matched image is built and reviewed, a short note goes to him (item walleye-ufs-go-note-for-author): how close the image is to Android's path step by step, what is still unknown (UFS_HW_VERSION, read only in our own init), and the remaining risk in plain words. Until his go: no UFS-on image is booted, the gate stays.
why: The author's words of 2026-11-19, relayed by the Top Coordinator: "or we can figure out how its done in android exactly and be atmost sure we understan the intricacies". The first decision named only the EDL way back or his explicit go; he added the second path today. The original 'Yes, wait' (2026-11-18) is unchanged as to the probe from our kernel on the phone.
rejected: Treating the second path as the go itself (he said 'figure out' and 'be at most sure', and the final go is his); lifting the gate when the builder or the programmer review says it is close (the gate is the author's, not a session's); dropping the EDL path (still valid, still unknown)

brief: The card's RST_n pulse: raise the msm8998 tlmm ngpios to 154 and give ufshc reset-gpios <tlmm 153>; reserve the three sdc2 pads
decision: The matched UFS image pulses the card through mainline's reset-gpios path: pinctrl-msm8998 ngpios 154 (UFS_RESET is pin 153), gpio-ranges 0 0 154 and gpio-reserved-ranges 150 3 in the overlay, reset-gpios <&tlmm 153 GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW> on ufshc. ufshcd_init pulses it (10-15 us each way) before it enables the host.
why: Mainline's own path, the sdm845 precedent (same UFS_RESET macro, oe_bit -1, same reset-gpios); no new code in the host driver. Pins 150-152 become gpio lines and are reserved, so nothing can drive their pads.
rejected: pinctrl states dev-reset-assert/deassert as the vendor does (needs a new driver path: mainline's host driver takes a gpio, not states); a ufs-qcom fix that writes the pad register directly (hidden hardware access); no pulse (leaves abl's card state, which Android never does)

brief: The matched UFS image leaves out ICE, bus votes, PM-QoS, hw-gated clocks and Android's link-startup pre-change: it matches the card-facing parts
decision: The matched image carries what touches the card and the PHY: quirks, purge guard, PHY table by version, RST_n pulse, the l26 rail always on. It does not carry ICE, bus votes, PM-QoS, hardware-gated clocks, the pad drive/pull of ufs_reset, nor Android's link-startup pre-change (RX line config, PA_VS_CONFIG_REG1 mask, hw clock gating before link startup), and mainline's clock scaling and other host caps stay.
why: Mainline has no MSM8998 ICE node or binding and ICE cannot touch the link or the card's identity; bus votes and PM-QoS are performance; the link-startup pre-change would be new host-driver code for a probe that is not yet allowed. The image says it matches the card-facing parts, not all of Android's path.
rejected: writing the link-startup pre-change now (new code before the author's go, unreviewed hardware access); calling the image a full match (it is not)

brief: A UFS host version the PHY refuses stops the probe at init, before the card reset and the host enable
decision: ufs_qcom_init hands the version it read to the PHY (phy_configure); the MSM8998 PHY accepts 3.0.0 and 3.1.0 only and answers -ENODEV, so the probe fails there. The same call stays in the power-up sequence.
why: The programmer review showed the host enable ignores a failed power-up pre-change, so a refusal there was not a stop.
rejected: refusing only in the power-up sequence (the host is enabled anyway); a version check in the PHY's power_on (same problem)

brief: Display bisect d1 and d2 are cut from the dtb inside boot-display.img; the panel's remote-endpoint goes with the panel node
decision: d0, d1, d2 are lpoco-bringup series images on z21's boot.img (build/series/display-bisect.toml). Image.gz and the dtb are cut from boot-display.img (ed155326, clock_gcc on the real gcc); d1 = mdss and display controller okay, DSI and PHY disabled, panel node and the DSI output's remote-endpoint removed; d2 = d1 with DSI and PHY okay. images-display/msm8998-google-walleye-display.dtb (84c72763) is not stale for the build: build-display-image.sh reads it as the raw input and fdtputs clock_gcc; no bisect image reads it.
why: Cutting from the image makes the parts the very bytes the tried d3 boots, so a difference is the stage and nothing else; checked by decompiled diff, and check-display-bisect.sh reads the stage dtbs and the display kernel itself.
rejected: Rebuilding the dtbs from the dts: a second route to the same bytes with a chance to differ; leaving the dangling remote-endpoint: it names a phandle of a node that is gone; deleting the raw dtb in images-display: build-display-image.sh needs it

brief: The display bisect runs unattended and is read from the console and logs; the author is asked to look only once an image boots with a working console and the DRM state read
decision: Images d0, d1, d2 are tried one by one from slot b with no person at the phone. Per image the keeper records, from machine witnesses only: whether the USB gadget (1d6b:0104) enumerated and when (host kernel log), whether the mainline shell (telnet 172.16.43.1, no password, tests/host/mainline-shell-read.sh) answered, its dmesg with the DPU, DSI, PHY and panel probe lines and the DRM connector status, and when Android came back (seconds after leaving fastboot) with /sys/fs/pstore and the boot reason read from Android afterwards. The crashing stage is named from these. Only when an image that carries the panel boots, has the working shell, and its dmesg, probe lines and connector are already read, the keeper asks the coordinator to ask the author to look, for the stripes alone.
why: The author, 2026-11-19, relayed by the Top Coordinator, verbatim: "can they first make sure it boots and they have console then ask me to look ?". After try 1 his eyes gave one fact (logo, then black, then Lineage in under a minute) and the cause could not be read from it; the shell is the witness that works (z21 and upstream-dts: gadget 18 s after fastboot). The mainline shell needs no root and no ssh password (telnet on usb0), so there is no access to add: try 1 had no console because the kernel never got to the gadget.
rejected: Asking him to watch the panel for each of d0, d1, d2 (his time, and his eyes cannot name a probe stage); reading the cause from the logo-then-black alone; adding a root or password route to the image (not needed, and against the lane's rules); another try of the full display image before the stage is known

brief: Find why d1 dies by loading the display driver late from the shell with the log streamed, not by more node-split images
decision: Build the display path as modules, keep d1's dtb, add netconsole, and load the modules by hand with the kernel log already going to the host over usb0 (netconsole and a TCP dmesg stream). One try reads the last logged step. Node-split images (mdss alone, display-controller alone) stay as the fallback if the late probe cannot carry a log.
why: Research walleye-display-bisect-d1-loses-the-shell: d0 boots, d1 does not, and the kernel dies before userspace so no log survives; every channel that outlives a hang is closed (pstore needs root and every mainline try left it empty, no UART owned, the vendor kernel as instrument cannot show our probe). A node split says WHERE (one more image per node), not WHY; the late probe says why in one try, and the same image carries later stages (dsi, panel) behind the same hand-loaded steps.
rejected: More node-split images first (two or three tries to learn a node, no mechanism); ramoops/pstore (needs the author's unlock and root; empty after every mainline try); a UART (not owned: walleye-get-uart-setup waits for his purchase); asking the author to watch the panel again (his words: console first)

brief: UFS is the lane's own work: get all Android can give, extract a working solution, then bring the author the go note; nothing waits on him holding it back
decision: The UFS try waits on the Android-derived solution, which is the lane's work: the gap items walleye-ufs-gap-* (version, link-startup pre-change, ICE, the bootloader hand-over, lane 1, Sony's mechanism, bus votes and pad drive) and then walleye-ufs-solution-extracted, which refreshes the go note. When that exists the note goes to the author, and his word opens walleye-try-ufs-match. Until then no UFS-on image is booted (the gate stays). Items, waits and reports say 'waits on the Android-derived solution (the lane's work)', not 'the author holds it'.
why: The author, 2026-11-19, relayed by the Top Coordinator, verbatim: "im not holding it back, im waiting until we have all we can from android and a working solution that is extracted from that as we were discussing before". The earlier wording (waits on his go, parked) made the work look held by him; it is waiting on us. The parts behind UFS (audio, haptics, radios, Wi-Fi) keep moving on research while it does.
rejected: Leaving UFS parked until he asks (the lane would idle on what is its own work); starting the try now on the matched image because he is not holding it back (the solution and the go note are not there yet, and the gate is the lane's safety)

brief: Do not carry Android's RX linecfg and PA_VS_CONFIG_REG1 mask into the matched image; mainline's link startup stands; fallback is one reviewed PHY write if the try's link fails
decision: The matched image keeps mainline's link-startup path. The try's reader also prints PHY+0x130 (RX LineCfg disable bit) to answer the one unknown.
why: Mainline Qualcomm hosts incl. the sdm845 PHY table MSM8998 uses boot UFS without these steps; the two are not needed for link-up; decision no-ice-no-linkstartup bars new unreviewed hardware code.
rejected: Carry both steps now: new hardware writes on a phone with a known bricking record, no evidence they are needed. Carry RX linecfg alone: same, with an unknown default that one read settles first.

brief: The late-probe ramdisk is z14's init with one change: its 180 s self-reboot is held while /tmp/hold exists
decision: init-late = init-z14 whose petter loop reads 'while [ $n -lt 90 ] || [ -e /tmp/hold ]'; the host script touches /tmp/hold the moment the shell answers. The kernel tree for the late-probe build is the fuel-gauge worktree (wt-k-fg), the fuel-gauge driver left off.
why: The display modules, loaded one at a time with a pause between, outlast z14's fixed 90 beats; without the hold the init reboots the phone mid-probe and the log would end at the timer, not at the fault. The shared dts names the label pmi8998_fg, defined only by the fuel-gauge dtsi patch, so the older display worktree no longer compiles it.
rejected: A new init beside z14's with the loader inside it (the host script drives each step, so the init stays dumb and the steps stay in a host file written before each load); lengthening the 90 beats (still a timer the probe can outrun); patching the pmi8998_fg label out of the dts (a second dts for one try)

brief: The display death is in the dtb, not the kernel (d0 boots with the DRM drivers built in); split the dtb's additions with the late-probe kernel
decision: Four images on the late-probe kernel: f0 z21's dtb (control), f1 the regulator additions only, f2 the pinctrl states only, f3 the display nodes (mdss, display-controller, dsi, phy) okay only; tried once each, f0 first, all four even after a failure. The late-probe kernel-with-nodes-disabled the keeper suggested is f0; a ramoops read stays closed (needs the author's unlock and root; empty after every mainline try).
why: Facts: d0 = display kernel with DRM built in + z21's dtb boots a shell (335 dmesg lines, PR 408); d1 = same kernel + the display dtb with mdss and the display controller okay loses the gadget; the late-probe image (DRM as modules that never load, netconsole, init-late) + d1's dtb also loses it (PR 418). A built-in DRM kernel survives with z21's dtb, so the kernel is not the cause; the dtb's additions are. The author, 2026-11-19: console first, then ask him to look (decision 2026-11-19-walleye-display-console-before-eyes); the black screen he saw (research walleye-display-try1-author-saw) is consistent with a panel rail being cut, which f1 tests, but it is a guess until f1 is tried.
rejected: Another kernel variant first (d0 already shows the kernel is fine); the ramoops read (root and unlock needed, pstore empty every time); asking the author to watch the panel (his words); stopping at the first failing image (the three groups are independent, one run answers all)

brief: The author is asked to attend only when the try is one command away: one Rust program per try, dry-run and every unattended part already run for real
decision: Every attended try of this lane (display stripes, touch z21, PMIC v1 reboot-then-bite, any later UFS try) becomes ONE program with ONE command, its logic in Rust (a rust-script, a small crate of this lab, or an lpoco subcommand where lab-tools already has the piece) - not shell. The program covers the whole sequence: the gate (tests/host/ufs-off-image.sh) and battery, the boot, the console and log reads, the pattern or the touch reader, the prompts to the author (what to expect, what to check, the moment to act), the record of the result and the way back to Android. Its invocation surface is declared once with argenv (practice 43). It has a dry-run that prints and checks the whole sequence without booting, and a mode that runs every part that needs no person for real. Order per try: the program is built, dry-run passes, a keeper runs the unattended parts for real and records it, and only then the coordinator asks the author to attend: he says go and the one command runs (a keeper runs it, or he does). Until then the try item stays blocked and no person is asked. The programs build on lpoco-lab (fastboot, keeper, kernel) and tests/host readers by calling them, not copying; the older shell readers stay as they are (author, earlier: 'shell scripts stay as they are'). The entry file of each program reads like a checklist: one plainly named call per step (boot_image, read_dmesg, draw_pattern, ask_author("..."), back_to_android, ...), each stopping the run on failure, the whole procedure on one screen; plumbing, parsing and retries are kept in helper modules or lpoco's shared runner. The programs are written against the shared runner lpoco-attended (lab-tools, attended/): procedure, step, check, ask_author, phone(), with dry-run and the log from the library; the rust-script entry file takes it as a cargo git dependency at tag lpoco-attended-vX.Y.Z; our readers, parsing and retries are helper modules of this lab. CORRECTION (orchestration, 2026-11-19, lab-tools tag lpoco-v0.28.3, #243): the runner is released and lives in lpoco-bringup, NOT in a crate of its own: dependency lpoco-bringup = { git = "https://github.com/linux-phone-oco/lab-tools", tag = "lpoco-v0.28.3" }; use lpoco_bringup::attended::*; entry = procedure("name").run(|p| { p.step("..", phone("..").retry(3,1))?; p.ask_author("what to do", "what to check")?; p.check("..", phone("..").expect(".."))?; Ok(()) }); phone(..) runs as the phone user, phone_root(..) as root, sh(..) on the host; --dry-run, --log FILE, --help come from the library; copy bringup/examples/attended.rs. Where this paragraph and the older 'lpoco-attended' wording differ, this one holds. Device-agnostic steps keyed to bring-up step ids (boot_once, read_dmesg, check_probe, wait_for_usb, back_to_known_good) are coming in lab-tools: write ours inline for now and name the ones we would want in the library (note in the shared notes folder for orchestration). FINAL CORRECTION (orchestration, 2026-11-19, lab-tools #247, tag lpoco-attended-v0.29.0): the attended runner is its own crate again and the lpoco_bringup::attended module is removed; this paragraph replaces the earlier two (lpoco-attended vX.Y.Z, then lpoco-v0.28.3). Dependency: lpoco-attended = { git = "https://github.com/linux-phone-oco/lab-tools", tag = "lpoco-attended-v0.29.0" }; use lpoco_attended::prelude::*; let _run = procedure("name", "google-walleye"); (keep it bound) then step("what", || ..), check("what", || ..) (returns (), bool or Result; false or Err stops and names the step), ask_author("what to do / what to check"), phone().sh(..) / phone().root(..), retry(tries, secs, || ..); --dry-run runs no closure; --log FILE; copy attended/examples/attended.rs. Library steps (boot_once, read_dmesg, check_probe, wait_for_usb, back_to_known_good) come next in lab-tools: write ours inline for now and tell orchestration which are needed (note walleye-to-orchestration-attended-steps-wanted.md).
why: The author, 2026-11-19, relayed by the Top Coordinator, verbatim: "please, ask me to attent only when everything is preped 1 launch sequence away with test sequences being prepered as rust-script or something and they test them before asking me to attend". Today's attended tries cost him the visit and still failed for lane-side reasons (the touch window missed because the 'ready' arrived late; the display try with no console), which a sequence run for real beforehand would have shown. Practices 11 (a witnessed test: say what to expect, wait for the go), 21 (no shell past one-off glue; logic in Rust) and 43 (argenv) say the same. Second word, same day, verbatim: "make sure the rust program reads cleanly and simply on the top entry file level, like any other simple scripted procedure would read". Orchestration, 2026-11-19: the runner is written once for every lane (lab-tools builder, rank 1; first slice with those names, dry-run and an example).
rejected: Asking him again with the shell sequences as they are (the same misses); one big generic framework first with the tries after (the first plan is the display's, the framework grows out of two plans, not before); a program that skips the person's prompts when unattended (the prompts are dry-run, and the unattended run reads every part that needs no person); Python (practice 21).; an entry file that holds the plumbing, the parsing or the retry loops itself (it would no longer read like the procedure it is); a runner of this lab's own beside the shared one (two copies of the same plumbing)
scope: walleye lane attended tries; surya's lane to be told by the Top Coordinator

brief: The matched image does not carry Sony's Hynix EXTEND_SYNC_LENGTH (0x48) or AVAILTXDATALANES: Android writes neither on this card
decision: Keep the matched image's quirk set at HOST_PA_SAVECONFIGTIME and the NO_PURGE guard. Do not add EXTEND_SYNC_LENGTH or AVAILTXDATALANES; the existing check (tests/host/ufs-match-android.sh) keeps them out. If the try's link fails at HS-G3, read link state and fall back as decision 2026-11-19-walleye-ufs-linkstartup-do-not-carry says; do not reach for the Sony quirk first.
why: Google's wahoo vendor driver never writes PA_TxHsG1-3SyncLength or AvailTxDataLanes and runs this card at HS-G3, 2 lanes; Sony's values are workarounds for other Hynix cards, and the erase mechanism is unpublished, so a Sony-only write is an untested difference and a risk without evidence it helps.
rejected: Carry Sony's 0x48 as a precaution: it differs from the only proven Android link and its link to the erase is a contributor's belief, not a trace. Carry only AVAILTXDATALANES: Android uses both TX lanes, forcing one moves away from it.

brief: Walleye haptics and speaker: write DRV2624 and a bypass-mode TAS2557 as small clean-room mainline drivers; speaker over ADSP/q6/MI2S first, WCD934x later
decision: Read first, no phone: the exact vendor audio routing and the minimal TAS2557 bring-up sequence. Then DRV2624 (input force-feedback, regmap, structured like drv2667) and TAS2557 (ASoC codec, DSP bypass, no firmware) as new clean-room drivers from datasheets and the GPL register use, each sent upstream. Speaker sound goes through ADSP remoteproc + q6 APR + quaternary MI2S + a machine driver on the sdm845 pattern; the WCD934x/SLIMbus codec (microphones) waits until the speaker is heard.
why: Mainline has neither chip's driver and no sibling has one, so something new is unavoidable; the smallest honest piece first gives certain progress. The speaker does not touch the WCD934x (amps sit on MI2S), so the codec, the longest and least known part, is not on the path to a first sound. Bypass mode needs no Android firmware, which keeps it upstreamable (mainline-first) and clean-room. Sources: research walleye-audio-haptics-ways.
rejected: Port the vendor tas2557 driver whole with its DSP firmware loader: large, needs Android firmware files, cannot go upstream. DRV2624 through drv260x/drv2667 by adding a compatible: register maps differ, a patch would pretend otherwise. PMI8998's built-in haptics: disabled on walleye, the actuator is on the DRV2624. WCD934x/SLIMbus first: longest unknown, and not needed for the speaker. Tfa989x for the amp: the chip on walleye is TAS2557 (tfa98xx is in the vendor tree but disabled).

brief: Walleye audio and haptics: take porthole's drivers and dts piece by piece onto our kernel, one try per piece, instead of writing new clean-room drivers
decision: Replace the plan to write DRV2624 and a bypass TAS2557 from scratch. Take porthole's patches for the Pixel 2 XL one group at a time onto our kernel, in this order: DRV2624 (0018, with its dts node) as the smallest proof; then ADSP, q6 and the sound card (0084, 0085, 0159); then TAS2557 (0024, 0162, 0171-0174) with its firmware file; WCD934x microphones and voice last. Each group is a second boot entry tried by the keeper and proved by a heard tone or a read register. Whether to ship the vendor TAS2557 blob is the author's question, put in the backlog.
why: Porthole has them working on the same SoC family and the lab already boots its kernel; practice 13 says build on what exists. The TAS2557 needs its firmware, which settles the unknown that the bypass plan rested on. The earlier decision rested on a research row that missed porthole.
rejected: Writing both drivers clean-room (the superseded decision): duplicates working code, and bypass mode is not a known way. Adopting all 263 patches whole (decision of 2026-11-18): still rejected, taimen-focused and one untested walleye board; only audio groups are taken. Waiting for mainline: neither driver is upstream.

brief: The display nodes kill the boot through the SMMU: test f3 with iommu.passthrough=1 and without the mdss iommus property
decision: Test the reading that enabling the mdss node (which has iommus = <&mmss_smmu 0>) makes the SMMU put the display stream in a translating domain while the bootloader's scan-out is live, so the CPU is stuck in a context-fault storm until the SoC watchdog restarts the phone. Images g1 (f3 + iommu.passthrough=1), g2 (f3 without the mdss iommus property) and g3 (mdss alone) are tried once each, g1 first, unattended. If g1 or g2 keeps the shell, the late-probe try runs on it. RESULT (PR 440): g1 and g2 boot a shell, g3 does not: the mdss iommus property is what kills the boot (confirmed by images, the fault log not yet read). The late-probe images L1 and L2 carry it forward.
why: Facts: f0, f1, f2 boot (dtb groups regulators, pinctrl are innocent); f3 (mdss, display-controller, DSI host and PHY okay) does not, with every display driver a module that never loads, so the death needs no driver: it is a device existing in the tree. The mdss node has an iommus property; the SMMU at cd00000 probes in d0 with 'preserved 0 boot mappings'; the bootloader's splash is on screen at fastboot boot; the author saw logo then black; Android came back 54-57 s after fastboot, the SoC watchdog's time, not a panic's. This is a reading, not a measurement: g1 and g2 are the test.
rejected: Only splitting the nodes (it says which node, not why; g3 keeps it); the ramoops read (root and unlock, empty every time); more kernel variants (d0 shows the kernel is fine); asking the author to look (his words: console first)

brief: The TAS2557 firmware is the phone's own: read from its vendor partition into the lab's material, hashed, never put in a repository and never shipped by us
decision: The lab reads tas2557s_PG21_uCDSP.bin from the phone's own vendor partition (a keeper, read-only, unattended), keeps it in ~/lab-material/walleye (not git), records its sha256 against porthole's copy, and loads it on the phone at boot from the phone's own partition, as the lane already does for the Wi-Fi firmware (device.toml [layer] firmware: extract-from-partitions). Nothing of the blob goes into a repository, an image kept in git or a package we publish; so the question whether to ship the vendor blob does not arise now. The porthole patches for DRV2624, ADSP/q6, the sound card and TAS2557 are taken as GPL-2.0 kernel code with their authors' headers and sign-offs kept (the clean-room line of this lane allows GPL sources, observed behaviour and specs; it forbids proprietary code and blobs in git).
why: The lane's firmware policy (device.toml [layer], the Wi-Fi item: the firmware is the phone's own, read from its partition at boot, never in a repository). Research walleye-audio-haptics-porthole-has-it: the amp stays mute without the file, porthole fetches it from a mirror, the phone's vendor partition holds it too. The porthole drivers are ported from the downstream driver, which is GPL-2.0 kernel code. So no author decision is needed for what we do; a later decision to ship the blob would be his.
rejected: Putting the blob in a repository or a published package (proprietary, and the licence is not ours); taking the copy from a mirror (the phone's own partition is the source and avoids the mirror's provenance); asking the author now (nothing we do ships it); writing a bypass TAS2557 driver (the amp is mute without its firmware, research walleye-audio-haptics-porthole-has-it)

brief: The porthole audio port is atomized: one series per chip, binding, driver and dts apart, authorship kept, a per-chip record for any phone, proof steps keyed to device.toml
decision: DRV2624, TAS2557 and the q6/ADSP groups are each one series of separate patches (binding, driver, walleye dts), each upstreamable alone, porthole's authorship kept and our changes as separate commits on top. Per chip a record is kept of what any phone would need: part number, the driver's standing (mainline, porthole, ours), firmware (the phone's own, never in git), quirks, the proof test and the bring-up steps it covers. The proof steps are small library steps (lab-tools, docs #638) with walleye's values in device.toml; walleye-only scripts are written only where no library step fits and are named as wanted.
why: The author, via the Top Coordinator, 2026-11-19: parts atomized and easy to follow so they can go upstream and be useful for any phone; orchestration is researching where chip-level knowledge lives, so the port is shaped to fit whatever comes out of that.
rejected: Taking porthole's patches as one lump onto our kernel (not upstreamable, hides authorship); walleye-only proof scripts (not reusable by other phones)

brief: The touch try opens its reader first, shows EVENTS-READY, then asks the author; its window is what the phone's own restart leaves
decision: One Rust program per try: tests/attended/touch-try.rs (13 named steps on the shared lpoco-attended runner) over the crate tools/walleye-tries (settings declared once with argenv as WALLEYE_TRY_* variables, telnet shell, reader thread, steps, stand-in phone tests). Order: battery, image hash, UFS-off gate, boot, shell, touch device listed (dmesg saved again after the probe), window checked, reader started, EVENTS-READY shown, then the author is asked; Android is awaited BEFORE the events are counted. The window is WALLEYE_TRY_WINDOW (120 s) cut to what z21's 180 s restart leaves after the device is listed (about 65 s at 107 s); under 40 s the author is not asked. No hold step: z21's init has none.
why: The author's words: ask him only when one command is away; the entry file reads like a checklist. The third z21 try missed its window because the reader closed before 'ready' reached him. z21's init does not hold (research walleye-z21-init-has-no-hold). The programmer's review found the first hold and deadman code was a shell syntax error and unneeded on z21, so it was removed.
rejected: A hold and a phone-side deadman: dead code on z21 and wrong as first written (item walleye-z21-hold-init if 90 s is wanted). Porting touch-read.sh with a fixed 90 s window: the phone restarts before it ends. Sending 'ready' to the coordinator as a message: the program prints the prompt where the author reads it. A cleanup in the runner: it ends the process on a failing step. An unattended switch: stdin from /dev/null does it.
scope: walleye lane builders and keeper

brief: L4 is L3 with the four overlay pinctrl labels naming real tlmm groups, not a function-trace image
decision: Build L4 as L3 plus, in the display dts, the labels mdss_dsi_active, mdss_dsi_suspend, mdss_te_active, mdss_te_suspend on the real tlmm groups (mdss-dsi-active-state, mdss-dsi-suspend-state, mdss-te-state) and no stub for them. Drop the function_graph trace image. Gate: tests/host/dtb-display-pinctrl-labels.sh passes on the L4 dtb, then the one unattended try.
why: The defer is in pinctrl_bind_pins, before dsi_dev_probe (research walleye-display-dsi-defer-pinctrl-stubs): the vendor overlay hangs pinctrl-0/1 on our dsi node, pointing at stubs with no pin controller. Proven on the host by fdtoverlay and a failing test; no phone needed to name it. The trace image would have named the same site at the cost of a kernel with ftrace and a try.
rejected: The planned L4 with FTRACE and function_graph retval: names a call we now know without it, needs a kernel rebuild, a try, and tracefs the late-probe kernel does not have. Deleting the overlay's pinctrl properties in the dtb with fdtput: the bootloader merges the overlay after our dtb, so the properties come back. Removing the stub container: the overlay merge needs every label to exist. Applying the vendor groups to the dsi (naming a default state): two owners for gpio94, and the panel's own pinctrl already owns the pins.
scope: walleye lane: builder (L4 image), keeper (the try); build/gen-overlay-stubs.sh

brief: Walleye radios: modem and SLPI sensors first (remoteproc proofs), NFC next, camera last; fingerprint waits on identifying the chip; deep sleep on Android's baseline
decision: Order by certain progress per cost: 1 modem remoteproc proof, 2 SLPI boot + qrtr sensors, 3 NFC node, 4 deep sleep (Android baseline, then cpuidle), 5 fingerprint identification, 6 camera port. Each first step is a host-side read or a read-only proof by the keeper; all wait behind walleye-ufs-readonly where they need partitions. Failing tests in tests/health/base: nfc-present, camera-sensor-present, slpi-sensor-service, suspend-residency. Backlog: walleye-modem-mss-proof, walleye-slpi-boot-qrtr, walleye-nfc-nxp-nci-node, walleye-deep-sleep-baseline, walleye-fingerprint-identify, walleye-camera-camss-diff.
why: Rests on research rows walleye-modem-way, -sensors-way, -camera-way, -nfc-way, -fingerprint-way, -deep-sleep-way: modem and SLPI drivers are upstream and a sibling phone (OnePlus 5) or the SDM845 recipe shows the path; NFC is a mainline driver plus a dts node; the camera needs a new camss port (40-80 h) and a VCM driver nobody has; fingerprint and deep sleep have an unknown a cheap read settles first.
rejected: Direct i2c sensor drivers (the SLPI owns the buses, probably); PN80T secure element (closed); fingerprint userspace SPI driver now (protocol proprietary, TEE-gated); libhybris/Android HAL for the camera (not upstreamable, against the mainline goal); modem IPA data first (unstable on OnePlus 5)

brief: Walleye fingerprint: probe the FPC sensor's HWID over SPI from a test kernel first; no userspace driver until that answers
decision: After identification, queue one phone try (walleye-fingerprint-spi-hwid, rank 95, after UFS, modem, sensors) that reads the HWID over SPI. Build a libfprint/userspace driver only if it reads; if TrustZone blocks the bus, record fingerprint as not possible on mainline for now.
why: The dtb gives irq, reset and supply but not the bus; the biggest unknown is bus and TZ lock, and it is settled in one cheap try. emainline shows the approach works on a sibling SoC.
rejected: B full libfprint driver now: protocol and image capture unknown, large work resting on an unsettled lock. C defer with no step: loses the cheap answer. Treating the press report (CrucialTec) as the chip: it is the module maker; the dtb says FPC.

brief: Walleye's TAS2557 series starts from Boiano's v3 (binding + driver); porthole's port stays a fallback, mined only for what v3 lacks
decision: Build the TAS2557 series from Boiano's v3 on linux-sound: patch 1 the binding as posted, patch 2 the driver as posted, patch 3 walleye's dts as one node, reg = <0x4c>, <0x4d>, reset-gpios, the four supplies, firmware-name only if v3 does not pick tas2557s_PG21_uCDSP.bin itself. Carry v3 as FROMLIST. Porthole's 0024/0162/0171-0174 are not applied; they stay a reference for gaps (PGID-based firmware choice, volume controls) that a measured try shows v3 lacks, each such gap a separate small patch. A walleye result, good or bad, goes back to the list in the author's name. Amends the order of 2026-11-19-walleye-audio-from-porthole for this chip only; the other groups still come from porthole.
why: Practice 13 and upstream-first: v3 has a reviewed binding (Kozlowski), supports exactly walleye's shape (two amps on one reset, stereo firmware), and is Boiano's own code; porthole's has no binding, a one-node hack that cannot pass review, and is declared ported from the downstream driver. The author asked for one series per chip, each patch upstreamable (decision 2026-11-19-walleye-audio-port-shape). The risk is that v3 is unproven on msm8998 and still under review; one build and one boot try settle that, and porthole stays as the fallback.
rejected: Porthole's port as the base: not upstreamable (no binding, hardcoded second address), LLM-assisted and downstream-derived, but proven on a Pixel 2 XL: kept as fallback and reference. Writing our own driver: duplicates two existing ones. Waiting for v3 to merge: the list gives no date and the series needs the firmware file anyway; carrying v3 costs nothing.

brief: The attended tries read their settings from device.toml (dev/proc at the top of main); no WALLEYE_TRY_* variable is left
decision: Every setting of tools/walleye-tries is a key of device.toml in the table that owns it ([connection] shell_address/shell_port, [tools] adb/fastboot, [boot] device_wait/back_wait, [images] dir and [images.z21|wdt1-a|wdt1-b], [procedures.touch-events-on-z21] and [procedures.pmic-watchdog-v1-on-the-pixel-2]); Settings::for_touch/for_pmic read them through lpoco-attended v0.32.0 dev()/proc() right after procedure(); Settings::read takes the two reads as functions so the stand-in tests run the same code. [kernels] test/kept and the gadget usb_id 1d6b:0104 are declared. The images are the rebuilt sysfs-less pair. The out folder and the lpoco program name are no device fact: fixed in code, a test sets them.
why: Item walleye-try-settings-into-device-toml; orchestration's map (docs #662) and lpoco-attended v0.32.0 rules.
rejected: Keeping env overrides beside the keys: two sources for one fact, the item forbids it. Image names wdt1_a/wdt1_b: the manifest allows lowercase, digits and - only, so wdt1-a/wdt1-b. Absolute or ../ image paths: the manifest forbids both, so [images] dir is build/images, a gitignored link to ~/Projects/walleye-build. A split Settings per try: 50 uses in tests for no gain now; the other try's fields stay empty.

brief: The stripe drawer puts the console in KD_GRAPHICS (KDSETMODE on /dev/tty0) while the stripes are held, and back to KD_TEXT after the release
decision: walleye-stripes opens /dev/tty0, sets KD_GRAPHICS before the first write, and sets KD_TEXT again after the release and clear, also when the draw failed; its log also carries /proc/consoles and each /sys/class/vtconsole/vtcon*/{name,bind}. The pan, the forced set_par and the unblank stay. Proposed for the builder; nothing on the phone is changed by this decision.
why: The v7.3 source shows the drawer's own FBIOPUT_VSCREENINFO repaints the console over the stripes (fbcon_modechanged -> update_screen), and every fbcon repaint path returns early in KD_GRAPHICS; the ioctls all returned 0 and the author saw a red-blue-green blip, so the commit path works.
rejected: Unbinding fbcon (vtcon bind=0): also silences it but detaches the console from every fb for the rest of the boot, bigger than the question needs. Drawing through the DRM master: right for a compositor later, a new program for a question the fbdev path answers. Dropping FBIOPUT_VSCREENINFO alone: the next console write or unblank still repaints.
scope: tools/walleye-stripes, procedures/display-stripes-on-the-pixel-2.rs, the builder, the keeper's try

brief: Settle the B1 backlight -110 by a sysfs brightness write after boot, then move the first 0x51 write out of the first-frame window
decision: Step 1 (read only, keeper's next B1 visit): after boot write /sys/class/backlight/*/brightness and read dmesg; it settles A versus B/C. Step 2 if it works: the driver defers the first 0x51 write (delayed work after the first pp-done, or brightness left to userspace), no flash. Step 3 if it fails again: look at TE and MDP clock/bandwidth votes (B, C). The -110 is not a boot blocker: drm_panel_enable only logs it.
why: The source read gives one mechanism, a DMA command racing the first MDP frame, with two sibling causes; one idle write tells them apart at no cost to the phone.
rejected: Ignore it as a log line: the glass may stay dark. Patch the msm dsi host first (wait for MDP idle): upstream code and a larger change before the cause is counted. Swallow the error in the panel: hides the failure and leaves brightness unset.
scope: walleye lane, phone keeper, panel-samsung-s6e3fa5

brief: Every walleye attended program and the walleye-tries crate pin lpoco-attended v0.35.1 together
decision: procedures/*.rs, tests/attended/*.rs, tools/walleye-tries and the CI install all name tag lpoco-attended-v0.35.1 (the newest, what the lab runs); a pin moves for all in one change.
why: The entry file and the walleye-tries crate each compile their own copy of lpoco-attended when their tags differ; the library's procedure() state is then two statics and the first step panics 'call procedure(name, device) before the first step' (seen on the B2 procedure at 0.35.1 against the crate at 0.32.1). 0.34 or newer was the instruction; the installed lpoco-attended is 0.35.1 and check --host reads device.toml with it.
rejected: Pin only the display procedure to 0.35.1: it panics at its first step against the crate. Pin to exactly 0.34.1: older than the installed binary and the lab's lpoco-lab, so check would run a newer reader than the programs use. Duplicate the crate per procedure: more code to keep in step for no gain.
scope: walleye lane, procedures, tools/walleye-tries

brief: L7's way back after any stop is the watching parent's reboot -f / sysrq, not the init's 600 s deadman or the drawer's own release
decision: The display look procedure is run as a watched child (walleye_tries::watch, as the UFS and PMIC tries): whatever ends it - an unanswered look, a failed check, Ctrl-C - the parent sends the phone back (reboot -f over the shell, then sysrq b, then the power-hold sentence). The shell hold's deadman is lengthened to outlast two answers (2 x 600 s).
why: B2's unattended run for real stopped at look 1 and the phone came back only by the init's deadman after ~10 minutes (PR 588): a person who answers late, or nobody, must not leave the phone on the test image. The watcher is the shared, tested way back.
rejected: Lengthening or shortening the init's own self-reboot: the image is L6's init-late, which must stay byte for byte (control); the deadman only covers a dead host. Relying on the drawer's end to release the hold: it never runs when look 1 is unanswered. A new way back in the procedure: the shared Lab::way_back already does it.
scope: google-walleye-lab display look; keeper's run

brief: B2's failures are the bootloader splash still live at 2 s: bisect the delay first, then reserve the splash region with simple-framebuffer in the dts
decision: Chosen vector: (1) bisect by load delay to find which cleanup ends the bootloader scan-out; (2) reserve memory@9d400000 no-map and a simple-framebuffer with the mmcc clocks and MDSS_GDSC in the walleye dts, as OnePlus 5/5T do; (3) only if faults remain, a dpu handover fix (disable autorefresh, wait idle, before the domain attach), upstream. Proof: health check display-boot-clean.
why: Four runs: loads at 2 s fail identically on all three signs, the load at 66 s with the same modules and order has none (research walleye-display-b2-dsi-clock-warning). walleye reserves nothing at 0x9d400000 though the faulting iovas lie there; other msm8998 boards reserve it.
rejected: Init waiting a fixed time: hides it, not mainline, kept only as a fallback. Reordering modules: L6 has the same order and works. Pixel-clock-only fix (H2): does not explain the SMMU faults. Removing iommu.passthrough: not the sole cause, L6 has it too.

brief: The delay bisect bakes each delay into its image as /display-delay, read by init-display-delay; five images, one unattended procedure
decision: Five images B-d5..B-d50 are B2 with /init = init-display-delay (init-display plus added lines: wait until /proc/uptime reaches the number in /display-delay, say it, then load) and one added file /display-delay. procedures/display-delay-bisect-on-the-pixel-2.rs boots them in a row from fastboot, scores the three signs per kernel log, goes back to Android between images and after any stop, keeps the table with the flip point. No person step.
why: The load time then does not depend on the shell (the gadget only comes up at about 18 s), so 5 s is a real 5 s; B2 is reproduced byte for byte as the control, so the only differences are the init and one file (research walleye-display-b2-dsi-clock-warning, decision 2026-11-19-walleye-display-early-load-splash-handover).
rejected: A host-side delay (shell loads the modules after N s): the shell is not up before 18 s, so 5 and 15 s could not be tried. A kernel command line parameter: changes the header words and the kernel line B2 is compared on. Editing init-display in place: breaks the byte-for-byte rebuild of B1 and B2. A Rust rewrite of the image build script: the B1/B2 build scripts are shell with checks; kept the shape, the logic that scores is Rust with tests.

brief: Do not rely on a delay: fix the handover in the dts (reserve the splash, simple-framebuffer), driver wait upstream if faults remain; the 17-23 s images stay unqueued
decision: The load delay is a lab aid only. Next step is walleye-display-splash-region-dts at the early load (2 s); if SMMU faults remain there, walleye-display-handover-driver. Narrowing images at 17, 19, 21, 23 s are not queued.
why: The logs show the flip is in the bootloader's scanout, not a kernel event we could wait on; a fixed 25 s delay would be a guess depending on an unmeasured bootloader idle timer.
rejected: Waiting a fixed 25-30 s at boot: hides the fault, depends on an unmeasured timer, delays the display half a minute. Narrowing images 17-23 s: only refine the timer, change no work. Waiting on an event: none found in the logs.

brief: walleye-tries tests: stand-in programs are written whole and unheld, and a stand-in phone's restart is a marker file, not a clock
decision: Test fixtures that are executed go through fixture::executable (new file, mode set at creation, synced, closed, then a bounded wait until no process holds it open); the way-back tests' idle-android check passes on a marker the stand-in phone writes when it restarts (fake::phone_marking), never after a number of seconds.
why: Seen failing: under 12 busy loops the sysrq test failed 2 of 12 runs, the fastboot host test failed 2 of 6 with Text file busy (a forking thread copies the open write handle into its child until exec), the reboot test failed once in 50. After the fix: 50 of 50 full-suite runs pass under the same load.
rejected: A retry around the exec or the test (hides the race, forbidden by the item); a process-wide lock around every Command spawn (about 15 production sites, changes production code for tests); longer clock margins (still a race on a loaded CI machine).
scope: tools/walleye-tries tests

brief: Hand the splash over by resetting the MDSS block at mdss probe (resets = <&mmcc MDSS_BCR>), proven by one RAM image at 5 s; read the DPU registers to learn what stops at 25 s
decision: First step: image B-r5 = B-d5 (not B-s5: the splash reservation and the unbound simplefb add nothing) plus resets = <&mmcc MDSS_BCR> on the mdss node, loaded at 5 s; signs counted as in the delay bisect (SMMU faults, rcg warnings, DSI -110). In parallel a read-only try: at 5 s and at 30 s read the DPU/INTF/pingpong registers of the live scan-out by devmem from the shell, to see what the 25 s flip turns off. If the reset leaves the signs, next is the driver quiesce (item walleye-display-handover-driver: dpu stops scan-out and DSI before msm attaches), sent upstream. The dts reservation of the splash stays out of the way until a simplefb driver is actually built.
why: The faults are the live scan-out meeting msm's new domain; the bootloader state, not the mapping, also breaks DSI (-110, rcg), and a mapping fixes only faults. The MDSS_BCR reset is a one-line dts change on code that already exists (msm_mdss_reset), reversible by RAM boot, and settles hypothesis A at once. Other boards avoid the problem instead of solving it.
rejected: Pre-mapping 0x9d400000 in msm's domain (iommu-addresses): the IOMMU core maps direct regions in default domains only, so it needs a new msm patch and silences faults only; kept as a later part. Waiting 25 s in the dts: a hidden timing, rejected before (2026-11-19-walleye-display-flip-dts-not-timing). Disabling mdss like Pixel 3: no display. Identity attach of msm: loses isolation, no upstream path. More simplefb work: no driver is built, so it holds nothing.

brief: Four bites on two images (wdt2-hard, wdt2-warm: the warm type comes from a qcom,s2-type property, hard by default); the author is asked first, before any bite, and only through physical steps
decision: The four bites run on two images built by build-pmic-wdt-v1.sh with INIT_NAME=wdt2: wdt2-hard is image A's kernel and dts with init-wdt2 (type 0x07), wdt2-warm is the same tree plus kernel/pmic-wdt-s2-type/ (the driver reads qcom,s2-type, hard when the property is absent, a type that does not read back fails the probe) with the property set to 1 in that image's dtb only. The driver property reuses the downstream binding's name and values (1 warm, 4 shutdown, 7 hard), so what boots is the shape a later upstream patch would have. init-wdt2 differs from wdt1 in three things: pon-regs reads the whole reason blocks, wdt-arm trusts the driver's read-back (probe) for any type, wdt-bite takes the timeout (the cable-out bites are armed for 45 s, the author's time to pull the cable). The procedure asks the author to stay with a finger on the power button BEFORE the first bite of every group (a phone that stays dark after a hard bite needs the press), so a run nobody answers ends there with every lab-only step done and the phone back on Android by the shared way back. The entry file runs on lpoco-attended 0.39.0 and reads its keys through its own runner; walleye-tries stays on 0.35.1 for the older entries.
why: The item asks for B as A with the S2 type changed 'the way such a property would work': a DT property read by the driver is that, and one dtb edit on the same kernel keeps A's rebuild identical (the generalised script reproduced the v1 pair byte for byte, 9dfea096.. and 15f5e97d..). The unattended keeper run must end at the first ask with the phone on Android: the z9 and the 2026-11-19 run show a bite can leave the phone dark, so the ask comes before the bite, never after it.
rejected: A second hard-coded constant in the driver (B differs from what would be sent; the item says not to); a module parameter (the driver is built in, the command line would carry it: a different shape from the one that would be mailed); re-using the wdt1 pair (its ramdisk reads seven registers and cannot name the reason blocks, and wdt-arm refuses the probe for type 1); asking the author after the bite only (an unattended run would leave the phone dark); free-text ask_author for the readiness ask (the brief says the author is asked only through the physical steps: confirm is one); bumping walleye-tries to 0.39 now (it would break the six entries pinned to 0.35.1; those are items walleye-procedures-on-v0-34 and -step-groups).
scope: google-walleye-lab: procedures, images wdt2-hard and wdt2-warm, build-pmic-wdt-v1.sh, init-wdt2 (built on the parked branch walleye-wdt-pon-bites-procedure, NOT landed: the images and the procedure are not on main)

brief: PROPOSED stages (his yes still waits): rootfs on the unused slot's system, booted from RAM; then flash boot; then mainline writes. The distro is TAKEN: Alpine minimal
decision: PROPOSED for the author, nothing is taken until he says yes. Stage 1 (rootfs-boots): read back the unused slot's boot, dtbo, vbmeta, misc, system, vendor with sha256 (tests/host/slot-readback-check.sh); build a UFS-root kernel and initramfs (root read-only, tmpfs overlay, no discard) and a minimal Alpine rootfs of under 2.5 GiB (the hardware-test layer: getty on the tty and ttyGS0, sshd over usb-network, no UI; decision 2026-11-20-walleye-distro-alpine-minimal); write it to the unused slot's system partition from Android over adb root; boot our kernel from RAM with fastboot boot; proof is ssh over usb-network and the health suite. Stage 2 (boots by itself): fastboot flash boot of that slot and set_active after the read-back, boot counting falls back. Stage 3 (writable): UFS try 2 for gear, then an rw mount with nodiscard and the purge guard, proving the bootloader files unchanged by sha256 after each write run. Never queued: any write to xbl, abl, tz, hyp or other bootloader partitions, the GPT, erase, purge.
why: Android already writes UFS, so the rootfs needs no mainline write; stage 1 changes nothing the bootloader sees and returns to Android by reboot; the Sony-class hazard (erase, purge, unmap) is confined to stage 3 where it can be guarded and measured; decision 2026-11-18-walleye-android-disposable-no-bricking makes Android disposable and bricking the one hard line; no EDL way back exists.
rejected: pmbootstrap-style flash_rootfs plus flash_kernel first (writes boot and rootfs with no read-back and sets the slot before the UFS read path under load is seen); userdata as the first rootfs (ends Android data, needed only for a phone-UI image); a new partition or GPT edit (the bootloader reads the GPT, no way back); loopback rootfs.img on userdata first (one more moving part, OnePlus 5 way kept for later); Nura first (device package nobody wrote, 6-8 agent-h and pmbootstrap not installed; kept as the author's later choice); mainline UFS write before the root is proven read-only (the one hazard class, nothing needs it yet). UPDATE 2026-11-20 (the author's distro word): Debian minimal is rejected for stage 1 (his choice: Alpine, where the upstream work goes); Nura/postmarketOS rejected (no walleye port, refuses AI-assisted contributions); a UI or phone shell rejected for the bring-up layer.
scope: walleye lane: keeper, builder; the author's yes

brief: The author says yes to install stage 1: Alpine build tools on the lab machine, the write of the Alpine image to the unused slot's system partition from Android, a read-only UFS-on boot from RAM
decision: The author, 2026-11-20, answered "yes" to the Top Coordinator's restated stage 1 (relayed by the Top Coordinator): step 2, install Alpine's build tools on the lab machine (apk-tools static or alpine-make-rootfs, qemu-user-static) and build plain Alpine minimal as the no-UI hardware-test layer; step 3, write that image from Android (adb root) into the system partition of the slot Android is NOT on, after reading current-slot and with the read-back backup in; step 4, boot our kernel from RAM with UFS on, mount that partition read-only with a tmpfs overlay, and log in over usb-network. NOT covered: flashing a boot partition, set_active, our kernel writing to the card, any GPT, bootloader, erase or purge, the userdata loopback. Stages 2 and 3 of decision 2026-11-20-walleye-install-in-stages-proposed (flash boot and switch the slot; our kernel writing to the card) still wait for his word. Each attended or irreversible step is brought to him as one command, tested first (decision 2026-11-19-walleye-attended-tries-one-command): items walleye-install-write-procedure and walleye-install-boot-procedure.
why: His word 'yes', just given, to the Top Coordinator's restated stage 1; the research walleye-install-stage-how-it-stands shows stage 1 changes nothing the bootloader sees and returns to Android by reboot, the write goes to a slot Android is not on, with the read-back backup as its way back.
rejected: A go for flashing boot, set_active, mainline writes, any GPT or bootloader write, erase or purge, or the userdata loopback (not asked, not given); opening the write for a keeper before the image and its one command exist (the author's rule: attend only when one command away).
scope: walleye lane: keeper, builder; the author's yes

brief: The Pixel 2's first installed system is plain Alpine, minimal, as the hardware-test layer: no Debian, no Nura, no UI, no phone shell
decision: The rootfs of install stage 1 is Alpine (apk, OpenRC, musl), minimal: getty on the tty (the display console) and on ttyGS0, sshd over the usb-network gadget, the Qualcomm services the steps need (qrtr, rmtfs, pd-mapper, tqftpserv when a step needs them; ModemManager later), and lpoco-health. No sxmo, no phosh, no UI. Its package list follows decision 2026-11-19-hardware-test-layer (docs): the hardware tests run with no phone shell as the product; the shell and UI are later layers. No firmware or modem data inside the image (it stays on the phone). The kernel is ours; the initramfs is ours (no mkinitfs, Alpine's or any). The stages and their yeses are unchanged and still wait for the author (decision 2026-11-20-walleye-install-in-stages-proposed). READING CLOSED (Top Coordinator, 2026-11-20): 'shell' in this project means a phone UI shell (sxmo, phosh, Plasma Mobile), not a command shell; 'just tty' is a text console with a login, so getty on the tty and on ttyGS0 plus sshd stays as listed.
why: The author, "ye, alpine sounds reasonable(no nura, if we dont loose anything by giving nura up. if its alpine upstream, why use nura at all ?)" and "we were planning to use no shells at all, just tty, why we bringup hardware side" (the author, 2026-11-20, relayed by the Top Coordinator). Recorded reasons (Top Coordinator): Nura's ports do not cover walleye; sxmo, phosh, qrtr, rmtfs, pd-mapper, tqftpserv and ModemManager are all packaged in Alpine; postmarketOS refuses AI-assisted contributions, so 'upstream' for this lane means Alpine and mainline. What we give up by leaving Nura: its pmbootstrap device-package route and a ready phone UI, which this stage does not use. The cost: an initramfs of our own (we already have one from the matched image) instead of mkinitfs.
rejected: Debian minimal (the research's recommendation, research walleye-install-stage-how-it-stands: debootstrap and qemu-user-static, smallest effort for ssh; the author chose Alpine because it is where the upstream work goes); Nura / postmarketOS first (no walleye port, a device package nobody wrote, pmbootstrap not installed, and postmarketOS refuses AI-assisted contributions); a UI or shell image at this stage (sxmo, phosh: the author's 'no shells at all, just tty' while the hardware is brought up); Alpine's mkinitfs (our initramfs mounts the UFS root read-only with a tmpfs overlay already, item walleye-install-ufs-root-image).
scope: walleye lane: builder (rootfs image), keeper; the Debian item is dropped

brief: The Alpine test layer: root has no password on tty0 and ttyGS0; sshd listens on 172.16.43.1 only and takes a key only
decision: In the hardware-test image root's password is empty (the consoles are the author's cable and screen), sshd (rootfs/overlay/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-lab.conf) listens on the usb address only with PasswordAuthentication no and PermitRootLogin prohibit-password; the one key goes in with walleye-rootfs --authorized-key FILE.
why: A getty login on the tty and ttyGS0 is what the author wants (the Top Coordinator's getty reading, 2026-11-20); a cable-only network must still not take a password, and no secret of ours belongs in a repository or an image (practice 9).
rejected: A root password in the image: a secret in a file that is copied around. Telnet as in the earlier test images: no login at all on a system that is meant to stay installed. An ssh key generated by the builder: creating an identity is the author's or the coordinator's word, not the builder's.
scope: walleye image, walleye-rootfs

brief: The UFS-root init mounts only the partition walleye.root names (system_a|b), read-only, refuses the running slot, and keeps a bounded watchdog petter
decision: build/initramfs-root/init takes walleye.root=system_a|system_b from the command line (the image bakes system_a: Android runs from b), finds the one partition with that PARTNAME, mounts it ext4 ro,nodiscard,noload under a tmpfs overlay and hands over with switch_root. It refuses (log line, then the phone restarts by itself) with no name, a foreign name, the slot of androidboot.slot_suffix, no partition or two. A petter in the new root pets /dev/watchdog for 900 s (longer while /run/walleye/hold exists), then the phone resets itself. The proof is QEMU on a loop-made GPT disk, no root needed.
why: The author's stage 1 yes covers a read-only mount of the unused slot's system and nothing the card could be written by; naming the slot on the command line keeps one image for both slots and the slot guard keeps it off Android's. A petter that never ends would leave a hung phone to a hand on the power key; QEMU showed the first petter never held the watchdog (busybox applets need argv0 busybox), so the test now checks a process holds /dev/watchdog and that the reset follows the hold.
rejected: mkinitfs / Alpine's initramfs (the coordinator said our own); mounting by a fixed device name (sda order is not stable on UFS); a loop-device chroot test (needs root; QEMU needs none and runs the real init); an endless petter (no way back); noload omitted (a journal replay writes).

brief: UFS try 2 reads the gear under load by a bounded O_DIRECT read of sda, and checks slot flags through a second fastboot visit
decision: Try 2 is the existing matched-image procedure on lpoco-attended 0.41.0 with new steps: gear+clock (power_info, devfreq cur_freq) idle, sampled during a read of sda (dd iflag=direct to /dev/null, timeout, device.toml lun/load_mb/load_limit), and 2 s after; sda's primary+backup GPT sha256 before/after; fastboot slot flags before and, after Android is back, once more in fastboot. Missing clock node is 'not known yet', never a fail; a read that ends before one sample is 'not known yet' too.
why: Upstreams coordinator wants the gear under load before an OPP-table patch (docs #714); the author wants one launch. Values live in device.toml, commands are built only from a validated sdX name.
rejected: Reading slot flags from adb props: they show no retry/unbootable flags. Hashing the whole disk: reads GBs for no gain. A fixed-time sleep instead of sampling: could miss the load window. Weakening the UFS-off gate: stays untouched, the go item is the one exception.

brief: Install stage 1 is one program: one dd to system_a|b, slot read twice, backup equal to the partition read now, read-back by sha256
decision: procedures/install-rootfs-on-the-pixel-2.rs (plumbing tools/walleye-tries/src/install.rs). Order: battery, backup whole, image declared, author told, fastboot read of current-slot, Android as adb root, stage the image and hash the copy, adb slot suffix equals fastboot slot, target partition read now equals the backup's sha256, ONE dd (bs 4096, count = the image's blocks, conv=fsync,notrunc) to by-name/system_<other>, read-back of the image's blocks equals the image sha256 (page cache dropped before every read), every other partition of slot-parts.list re-read equals its backup, staged copy removed, Android back. The write step re-checks slot agreement, partition name and image sha itself. The way back is leaving it: Android's slot is never written; the backup goes back by hand (dd of the stored file).
why: The author's stage 1 yes (2026-11-20-walleye-install-stage-1-go) and his rule: attend only when one command away, tested first. Review by the programmer subagent found no path to a wrong partition; its fixes (page cache, gate right before the write, count, non-empty list) are in.
rejected: An automatic restore on any stop (a second write nobody asked for, onto a slot that is not booted); bumping to lpoco-attended 0.42.0 (the other procedures pin 0.41.0 and share the library's types; 0.42 adds nothing this needs); typing the slot (it is read); a Python or sh writer.
scope: walleye lane: builder, keeper

brief: The author's go covers each step inside a stage he approved, and read-only tries of the same kind; his word is asked once per stage, never per step
decision: COVERED, no further ask: every step of install stage 1 (the boot of the UFS-root image from RAM, read-only, with the tmpfs overlay and the login over usb-network), and read-only UFS-on tries of the same kind (UFS try 2 runs after the stage 1 boot). STILL HIS WORD, once per stage and not per step: stage 2 (flash a boot partition, set_active) and stage 3 (our kernel writing to the card). NEVER: the bootloader, the GPT, erase, purge. THE BAR FOR RUNNING IS UNCHANGED: one tested command, rehearsed (every part that does not boot UFS-on run for real, check --host, dry run), and a way back; the coordinator opens the go on the item with a short until and a keeper runs it; the result goes to the Top Coordinator. Only the asking goes.
why: The author, "when its ready, you have my go, dont come back to me with go'es like this, blocking the process of bringing up with my go'es on every little step" (the author, 2026-11-22, relayed by the Top Coordinator). He said it after the stage 1 write: his go came back to him on every step and slowed the bring-up. Decision 2026-11-20-walleye-install-stage-1-go gave stage 1 its yes; this one says the steps inside an approved stage need no more.
rejected: Asking him again for each phone step inside stage 1 (what he asked us to stop); treating this as a go for stage 2 or stage 3 (his word: once per stage, those stay his); widening the go to anything that writes the bootloader, the GPT, erases or purges (never, by the lane's rule: there is no EDL way back); dropping the bar (a one-command, rehearsed, with-a-way-back run stays the condition for every run).
scope: walleye lane: keeper, builder, coordinator; the author's go

brief: The root boot carries its gates as its own steps, not [kernels] pre_boot, and logs in by its own ssh call
decision: procedures/rootfs-boots-on-the-pixel-2.rs boots the UFS-root image through Lab::boot_image after its own steps: battery, sha256, the slot guard (adb suffix = fastboot current-slot = the other slot of the image's walleye.root), the go for this sha256 on walleye-install-rootfs-boots-try. The login is ssh by the declared key from [procedures.rootfs-boots-on-the-pixel-2] (identity, ssh_user, ssh_port), after the lab's own gadget wait; the way back sends reboot -f over ssh, polled for a boot's length.
why: [kernels] pre_boot is global and gets no kernel name, so a UFS go gate there would stop every kernel; boot_once also checks the gadget serial walleye-first-boot while the Alpine gadget says walleye-alpine. The init's own slot guard fails open without androidboot.slot_suffix (PR 676), so the program carries it. Programmer review found no path to the boot without these gates.
rejected: pre_boot gate scripts (global, cannot tell the kernel); steps::boot_once (serial check fails on the Alpine gadget); changing [connection] to ssh/key (would switch the telnet tries' lpoco calls)

brief: A risky step needs no word of the author once research shows our code does nothing Android's kernel did not; bootloader, GPT, erase, purge never
decision: THE RULE: a step that waited for the author's approval because it is risky proceeds WITHOUT it once the research shows that our code does nothing Android's kernel (and OTA) did not do on THIS phone for THAT step. The comparison is recorded as research with its sources (clean room: read Android's kernel and drivers, never copy), and the step is ONE tested command, rehearsed, with a way back. The verdict goes to the Top Coordinator with the result, not as a question. IT COVERS stage 2 (flash our boot into the slot Android is not on, set_active with boot counting, the way Android's own OTA does it) and stage 3 (our kernel writing to the card exactly as Android's UFS path does, the purge guard kept): items walleye-install-stage2-android-comparison and walleye-install-stage3-android-ufs-comparison carry the verdicts. STILL NEVER, whatever the research says, because the phone has no EDL way back: xbl, abl and the other bootloader partitions, the GPT, erase, purge; if the work seems to need one, STOP and tell the Top Coordinator. THE LANE KEEPS BRINGING UP ON MORE THAN ONE FRONT, within 3 sessions (RAM), each part Android-derived and clean-room, mainlined as it proves out, along the chain to daily-usable-phone (firmware-reachable, remoteprocs, audio, Wi-Fi, modem, charging). READING OF 'NEVER THE GPT' (the Top Coordinator, 2026-11-22: the 'never' list was his wording, not the author's; he told the author, and if the author objects it stops): 'never the GPT' means OUR code editing the partition table: repartitioning, resizing, changing entries, types or names, or writing GPT bytes ourselves. The bootloader's own slot switch through fastboot set_active, the same operation Android's OTA uses on every update, is ALLOWED under this rule with the verdict of research walleye-install-stage2-android-verdict. CONDITIONS: (1) read and keep all slot flags and both GPT headers BEFORE (fastboot getvar slot-* for both slots, plus the read-only read-back of the GPT LUN headers); (2) set_active only the slot whose boot we just flashed and read back; (3) check AFTER that the only changes are the slot attribute bits and the expected type-GUID and boot-LUN switch the open ABL describes; (4) the way back is fastboot set_active to Android's slot (b), the same operation in reverse, REHEARSED before it is relied on.
why: The author, "ok, make sure the work continues on bringing up, not only on that direction but those after. if something is blocking by my aproval because its risky, they do as much as possible by reading android kernel, drivers, doing clean room reverse engineering and so on, and when we are sure our code doesnt do something that android linux kernel didnt, we proceed, and mainline the thing. if its done this way, if best that could be have been researched, considered and done, there is no need for my approval, when its already best possible, and when we pass storage question i think there should be less of such places in the future." (the author, 2026-11-22, relayed by the Top Coordinator). He gave it after the per-stage go: asking, even once per stage, still blocks the bring-up; the best that can be researched, considered and done needs no approval. It rests on decision 2026-11-22-walleye-author-go-per-stage-not-per-step, which it amends, and on the lane's rule that Android is disposable but bricking is the one hard line (2026-11-18-walleye-android-disposable-no-bricking).
rejected: Waiting for his word on stage 2 and stage 3 (what he asked us to stop, once the research is done); treating 'research done' as a go for anything that writes the bootloader, the GPT, erases or purges (never: no EDL way back); a verdict without sources or a way back (the bar is unchanged: one tested command, rehearsed, a way back); stopping the other fronts of the bring-up while storage is settled (he asked for the work to continue on more than one).
scope: walleye lane: keeper, builder, researcher, coordinator; the author's approval

brief: Alpine on the glass with UFS off: the system_a userland is a tar in the ramdisk, unpacked into a tmpfs after the modules load, then switch_root
decision: Image B-a5 = B-r5's kernel, dtb, header, size and 13 modules as they are; its ramdisk adds /userland.tar, read out of the ext4 image written to system_a (debugfs rdump under fakeroot, setuid/sticky bits put back from the inodes), unpacked by build/initramfs-ramroot/init into a tmpfs after the 5 s module load; built by tools/walleye-ramroot (Rust, argenv), twice identical, checked by what is in the image. Ramdisk 6.8 MB, image 33554432 B = the boot partition (0x2000000); fastboot takes 0x20000000. Deadman 300 s, held by /run/walleye/hold for the look.
why: The author wants to see the login on the phone before the housekeeping; stage 1's UFS-root image has no display, B-r5 has the display and UFS off. The tar from the very image on system_a is the same userland, so what the author sees is what stage 1 wrote.
rejected: Userland as the ramdisk's own files (no tmpfs, no switch_root): the brief asks for a tmpfs root. A bigger image than the partition: not needed. Rebuilding the rootfs by apk: needs the network and gives another sha256 than system_a's. A shell build script: new programs are Rust with argenv. A 900 s deadman: longer than the lab's way-back wait (review finding).
scope: walleye builder, keeper

brief: The glass's getty moves to tty1 (Alpine's own line) and the lab reads the screen's text (/dev/vcs) before the author is asked to look
decision: inittab runs getty on tty1, not tty0 (securetty has both); rootfs v3 and B-a5 rebuilt from it; the look procedure gains check 15: the active VT's text holds 'HOSTNAME login:', polled over ssh, kept in screen.txt; the read also keeps the active VT, /proc/consoles, ps with tty, inittab, cmdline. A failed check stops the run before the look.
why: The look at B-a5 saw boot text and a cursor but no prompt though check 14 found a getty on tty0; Alpine's default is tty1 with VT 1 the fbcon console. The cause is not proven (hypotheses: vhangup on /dev/tty0, wrong VT); the screen check is what proves or refutes tty1 on the phone, and its saved readings name the next cause if it fails.
rejected: Guessing both tty0 and tty1 getties (muddies what the check proves); patching inittab inside the ramroot init only (the UFS root needs the same line); changing [images.alpine-rootfs] v2 in place (it is what system_a holds from the stage 1 write; v3 is declared beside it and the next write takes v3).

brief: The init with the display is its own file, build/initramfs-root-display/init, equal to the root init plus the display block; the root init stays byte for byte until its own rebuild item
decision: U-d5 uses build/initramfs-root-display/init: the root init's text plus the display block (delay, module lines) and the 'handing over' line before the moves; tests/host/ufs-root-display-init.sh proves it is nothing else and runs every case of the root init's proof on it. build/initramfs-root/init is not edited, so [images.ufs-root] (c3373d71, the one a go names) stays reproducible.
why: The ufs-root image is declared by sha256 and a go names that sha256; editing its init would change what a rebuild gives. Item walleye-initramfs-root-say-before-the-moves rebuilds that image once on purpose; until then the display init carries the same fix.
rejected: Editing build/initramfs-root/init in place: a rebuild of c3373d71 would no longer match and the open go would name an image nobody can rebuild. Loading the display modules from the root's OpenRC after the hand-over: the glass would show nothing of the init and the delay of 5 s from uptime is not kept.

brief: The stage 2 boot image is its own row [images.ufs-root-booted-slot] and file; [images.ufs-root] (c3373d71) stays the stage 1 RAM boot
decision: build-ufs-root-image.sh gets BOOTED_SLOT=yes: the command line also carries walleye.booted-slot, the image is written as NOT-TO-BOOT-ufs-on-ufs-root-booted-slot.img in its own folder, declared as [images.ufs-root-booted-slot] (sha256 e337de53, root system_a: Android is on slot b). install-boot-on-the-pixel-2 and its rehearsal name that row. Only the slot-a variant is built.
why: The RAM-boot of stage 1 keeps the old guard (no word, the other slot) under a go that names c3373d71's sha256; one name per image keeps a go from covering the wrong bytes. The flashed variant is the only one that carries the word. Built twice from clean inputs: the same bytes; differs from the stage 1 kernel/dtb/header/footer in nothing; the new init alone changes e21ac306 (stage 1 variant with the new init, not kept).
rejected: Overwriting [images.ufs-root] with the new init: stage 1's go and its proof name c3373d71. Building a system_b variant too: Android is on slot b, the flashed slot is a; one more image is one more sha256 for a go to name, and the script builds it with ROOT_PART=system_b in one command when the slot changes. A word-less stage 2 init guess at the slot: the word makes the intent explicit on the command line.

brief: First fix: the rootfs sends 'bootloader' through reboot(2) RESTART2; no dts change; IMEM word and warm reset only if that one try still misses
decision: Put a small static reboot-with-command tool in the Alpine rootfs and use it in the stage 1 way back instead of busybox 'reboot bootloader'. Prove offline from the tool's strace-free text and the dtb check; try once in the RAM boot. Only if the bootloader still does not stop, add the syscon-reboot-mode IMEM node (0x146bf000+0x65c = 0x77665500) and reboot=warm, one change per try.
why: Busybox source shows the argument is dropped, so the existing dtb was never exercised; the PMIC byte already equals Android's (qcom-pon.c vs qpnp_pon_set_restart_reason); a userland fix is the cheapest, certain-progress step and settles the biggest unknown (does the PMIC byte alone work).
rejected: Adding the IMEM syscon node and warm reset first: two unproven changes at once, and the imem node is unneeded if the PMIC byte works. Kernel patch to pass a default command: hides the cause, not upstreamable. Writing the PMIC register by hand from userland (spmi debugfs): bypasses the driver we want to prove. Using fastboot-less way back only: stage 2 safety is the other item.
scope: walleye lane builder and keeper

brief: The first lists reproduce the shipped images from frozen refs of the series; the live lists follow the series tips and build the next images
decision: The images that have run (c3373d71 and the stage 1 proof, 461077869fb2, e337de53, built on the kernels e123d3bff and 3644090c7) are reproduced by FROZEN lists named for them (for example ufs-off-e123d3bff, ufs-on-3644090c7) in kernel/topics.toml, where the series topic/pmic-wdt-wake-in-suspend is pinned at the commit the image used (e123d3bff, kept as the pushed ref archive/pmic-wdt-wake-in-suspend-e123d3bff or a pin the rhizoid format allows: the builder reads rhizoid.md and the format first, and if the format allows no pin it asks the rhizoid lane rather than weakening the check); rhizoid assemble --reproduces says EQUAL for them against e123d3bff and 3644090c7.
