The LIVE lists ufs-off and ufs-on follow the branch tips (topic/pmic-wdt-wake-in-suspend 8b2283da3 with its two review fixes) and build the NEXT images; a next image gets its own stage 1 run under the standing go before anything flashes it. Stage 2 flashes e337de53 as built: its kernel is the frozen list's tag, so it is an int/ tag and rebuildable from the record, and it carries the kernel stage 1 proved.
why: The builder's step 3 (PR 787) says DIFFERS for both lists in drivers/watchdog/pm8916_wdt.c only: the series branch carries two review fixes (Stop the watchdog on reboot and unregister, 8b2283da3) over e123d3bff on which the images were built. The branch tip is the series that goes upstream; it must not be cut back to match an old image, and the two fixes belong inside the series (squashed for v2), not in a stacked topic. The record's job is to rebuild what RAN: that is a frozen list. The quality check the rhizoid lane named is a first list reproducing an image, and this gives it without rebuilding the stage 1 proof.
rejected: Splitting the two fixes into a stacked topic so the series branch can sit at e123d3bff: rewrites the upstream-bound branch for the sake of an old image and separates review fixes from their series. Rebuilding the shipped images on 8b2283da3 now: new shas, a new stage 1 run and a new go for each, the stage 1 proof (26 of 26) and the UFS try results no longer tied to a rebuildable kernel, and it delays stage 2; the next images take the tips anyway.
scope: walleye lane, builders, kernel/topics.toml

brief: slpi_mem is 0x94c00000/15 MiB with mba, video and ipa/gpu moved to the running layout; our ipa/gpu/wlan nodes inside it go
decision: In our dts: slpi_mem 0x94c00000 size 0xf00000; mba_mem 0x94500000/0x200000; venus_mem 0x94700000/0x500000; delete ipa_fw_mem, ipa_gsi_mem, gpu_mem, wlan_msa_mem and add the phone's 0x95b00000/0x100000 ipa/gpu block; enable remoteproc_slpi with firmware-name qcom/msm8998/google/walleye/slpi_v2.mdt; the firmware files come from vendor_a at image build, never git.
why: The firmware needs 15 MiB (research walleye-slpi-carveout-answer); the phone's own dtbo and fdt place it at 0x94c00000 and shift its neighbours; one self-consistent layout avoids overlap.
rejected: Keeping 0x94b00000 and enlarging to 15 MiB: overlaps the shifted video/ipa layout the rest of the phone's TZ/ABL expect, no evidence it is accepted. 0x94300000 (mainline): overlaps our video and mba nodes and is not the walleye layout. 7 MiB as the earlier row said: too small for the image.

brief: A silent shell during the UFS try's bounded read is a reading kept with its time; wait on a fresh shell to the read's limit plus 60 s; the read is 2048 MiB
decision: Step 16 of the UFS try asks the read's state on its own shell; a state read not answered is written to gear-load.txt with its time, the state shell is reopened, no gear read is sent on a silent shell, and the wait runs to load_limit + 60 s before the step fails. load_mb goes from 4096 to 2048.
why: Runs 1 and 2 both stopped at step 16 about 15 s after the read began (run 2 log: 1795420605 begin, 1795420620 FAIL at the 10 s state read) after eight answered samples: the silence is the load starving the gadget, not a gear fault. The logs carry only procedure lines, not the phone's own text, so the cause inside the phone is not known yet; the smaller read is a hedge, judged, not measured.
rejected: Raising the 10 s alone: still stops a run that the read would finish. nice/ionice on dd: not known to exist in the phone's busybox, untried. Dropping the load: the gear under load is what the try is for.
scope: walleye-tries, the keeper's UFS try 2

brief: One more read-only RAM-boot try, same image: ramped load (64, 256, 1024 MiB), 1 s polls with a timestamp line before each step, devfreq pinned low; stage 3 stays blocked
decision: Run ONE try with the same ufs-on image sha (read-only, nothing written, nothing flashed): the load is ramped 64, 256, 1024 MiB with a pause between steps; before each step the phone appends 'step N start, uptime' to a file in its RAM and the host polls the shell every second; the changed variable is the devfreq governor of 1da4000.ufshc, set to powersave (clock 50 MHz, gear 1) before the first step - the host reads the governor, the current gear and the clock before, and sets nothing else. Read after: how far each step got, whether the silence is by time (4.5 s) or by volume, whether it appears at gear 1. Branches: shell stays alive through 1024 MiB at gear 1 = cause is gear 3 or the switching (causes 1 and 3); then a second try with governor performance (pinned high, no switching) separates the switching (1) from the sustained rate (3); silent again at gear 1 at the same 4.5 s = not the gear: causes 2 and 4, and the next try moves the ufs irq (smp_affinity) and the usb irq to different CPUs, then reads the PON reason after the way back; a volume-by-time split without a hang at 64 and 256 MiB = volume. On the way back the keeper reads the PON reason (bite or not) as the item walleye-pon-reasons-after-a-bite-how-to-read says. The existing go covers the image sha only: this procedure change needs a new go line.
why: The three logs show one fixed place of failure (about 4.5 s, gear 3 held), the first switch cleared, the OnePlus 5 on the same node works: so one variable on the same image, with the load shaped to tell time from volume, spends the least risk for the most separation. The governor is a runtime sysfs write on the phone's RAM kernel: no flash, no card write, no new image.
rejected: A new image with a log to pstore: ramoops is not shown to survive the warm reset yet and needs the author's unlock; an OPP-table image (walleye-ufs-opp-table-image): a patch before the cause is known; a try with clkscale_enable=0: it scales UP (ufshcd_clkscale_enable_store calls devfreq_scale up), the opposite of the pin low asked; sustained writes (stage 3): blocked until this is understood; looking for the cause by reading Android's vendor ufs-qcom only: it cannot tell the OUR-side difference, and Android's behaviour is already compared (walleye-ufs-solution-table)
scope: walleye keeper, walleye coordinator

brief: Before changing the image, repeat the stage 2 try without a flash and read slot a's console from pstore on Android b; do not change kernel, init or cmdline on a guess
decision: The next move on slot a no-ssh is one try with no flash: set_active a, fall-back, pstore read before any reboot, plus the stock fdt's watchdog values. Candidates by rank: bootloader-armed watchdog, cold USB, then cmdline words, dtbo, AVB, init path. The result picks the one change that follows (for example petting or taking over the apps watchdog at the very start of the init, or a USB bring-up step).
why: Nothing says yet whether our kernel started; the same kernel ran from RAM with ssh in 12 s, so the cause lies in what a normal boot adds. bootreason=watchdog means a watchdog bit, which a missing gadget cannot cause alone.
rejected: Making a change now to arm/pet the watchdog from init (a guess, costs a flash and a go); lengthening the 170 s window (stage 1 needed 12 s); a fastboot-boot repeat (cannot show a normal boot's state).

brief: When the new slot gives no ssh, stage 2 sends the phone nothing for up to 420 s, reads the failed boot (pstore first) the moment adb answers, and only then runs the way back
decision: At step 21, after device_wait without ssh, the step calls only reads (adb get-state, fastboot devices) until adb says device or fallback_wait (420 s, the procedure table's key) is over; the first act on Android is ls -la /sys/fs/pstore and a cat of each file whole, then cmdline, bootreason, sys.boot.reason, slot suffix, verifiedbootstate, uptime, id; kept in failed-boot-read.txt (serial redacted) and printed. adb root (adbd only, not the phone) is asked once, only when the listing or a pstore file says Permission denied; what was read before it is kept first, and the second read waits for id 0. The step still fails; the watching parent's existing way back runs after. The same read is a read-only step of the rehearsal.
why: Run 4 lost slot a's console: the phone fell back to Android by watchdog in about 3 to 4 minutes, and the next restart cleared /sys/fs/pstore before anything read it (PR 849, PR 851). 420 s is the longest wait seen (about 4 min) with margin; it is in the procedure table because the manifest's [boot] table is lab-tools' typed one and takes no new key.
rejected: Sending the way back at once on a silent step 21 (restarts the phone and clears the pstore: run 4); adb root before the first read (restarts adbd mid-boot, is no read); a [boot] key (lab-tools' manifest refuses it); reusing back_wait 240 s (no margin); failing the step without the wait (the keeper had nothing to read)
scope: tools/walleye-tries flash_boot (stage 2 step 21), device.toml [procedures.install-boot-on-the-pixel-2] and the rehearsal

brief: The stage 2 debug image has its own init file, build/initramfs-root-debug/init: the root init plus two blocks behind the word walleye.debug; the run declares it by one line of device.toml
decision: build/initramfs-root-debug/init is the root init, byte for byte, plus two DEBUG blocks that act only with walleye.debug on the command line. With the word: busybox watchdog petters on every watchdog device (looked for again every second; timeout = the driver's max_timeout, at most 600 s), a USB gadget (ECM+ACM, 172.16.43.1, telnet root shell, no password) up before the card is touched, every init line in /tmp/walleye-debug.log, a refusal HOLDS (walleye.hold, default 900 s, longer while /tmp/stay) instead of restarting; after the mount the gadget stays walleye.debugwait seconds (default 20) for a login, is RELEASED (the root's own unit takes the controller), the petters go on through the hand-over and end in the hold script. Image [images.ufs-root-booted-slot-debug] ec741a98 (kernel, dtb, header, footer e337de53's); install-boot-on-the-pixel-2 and its rehearsal name it by one line each; every run's step 21 keeps the host's journalctl -k lines of 3-2 since the set_active in host-usb-log.txt and failed-boot-read.txt (usb_log_match in device.toml). Proof: tests/host/ufs-root-debug-init.sh (QEMU, dummy_hcd) and the root init's whole proof with this init in its place.
why: Run 7 left no trace: no USB device of ours for 67 s and a watchdog bite after about 35-40 s; the gadget is brought up by the Alpine rootfs after switch_root, so a failure before it looks the same as no kernel. An image that makes the normal boot enterable lets the next run say what happened instead of guessing, and covers the two top causes at once (a watchdog the bootloader arms and our init does not pet; a cold USB or root mount that fails).
rejected: Editing build/initramfs-root/init in place: e337de53 and c3373d71 would no longer rebuild (decision 2026-11-23-walleye-display-init-beside-the-root-init). Keeping the debug gadget after the hand-over: the root's own gadget unit would find the controller taken, and a root that mounts is the case we already know. Setting the watchdog timeout by hand with a shell loop only: the driver's own longest timeout is the margin when the init is slow. A fix of a guessed cause (watchdog, reboot reason, UFS) before reading: decision 2026-11-23-walleye-stage2-no-ssh-read-pstore-first.

brief: Clean-room only for sources we have no licence to; Android's Pixel 2 kernel (msm-4.4, GPL-2.0) may be reused with its copyright, author and Signed-off-by kept
decision: Clean-room reverse engineering is for sources we have no licence to: the bootloader, firmware blobs and closed userspace. Android's Pixel 2 kernel (msm-4.4, android-msm-wahoo) is GPL-2.0, so its working parts may be reused in our lab kernel, as a first working step by direct copy, and for upstream by a port onto mainline's interfaces. Rules: keep the original copyright and author lines; the commit message says 'based on FILE from ANDROID-COMMIT'; keep the original Signed-off-by where a commit is taken whole (DCO (b)); check each file's licence before it is copied (GPL-2.0 or dual BSD/GPL is fine, anything else is read for behaviour only). AOSP userspace (Apache-2.0, e.g. boot_control.cpp) is read for behaviour only and never goes into the kernel. Android's tree is held as a read-only remote 'android' of the kernel clone, fixed at the exact build the phone runs, tagged reference/android-walleye/BUILD, never merged into a topic and never pushed; findings cite android:path@commit from the local tree, not web pages. This supersedes any 'no vendor code is copied' line in briefs or research of this lane.
why: The Top Coordinator's decision with the author agreeing, 2026-11-23: 'isnt it the best we can do ?' (the author, relayed by the Top Coordinator): the kernel that runs on the phone works, is GPL-2.0, and reusing it with its authorship kept is what the licence is for; clean-room work stays where no licence exists. It also settles how the watchdog work reads msm_watchdog.c and the stock dts: from the tree, at the commit the phone runs.
rejected: Clean-room for the kernel as well (the author's words of 2026-11-22 spoke of clean-room reverse engineering where research could not reach: it is kept for the bootloader, firmware and closed userspace): it would re-derive working GPL code at the cost of time and bugs, with no licence reason. Merging Android's branch into a topic or pushing it to the fork: it is a reference, not our history.
scope: walleye lane, builders, researchers; briefs that say no vendor code

brief: The init reads the slot as Android does and the header command line is under a budget, never a hardcoded slot
decision: The header command line of a stage 2 image is under 160 characters and must leave 100 characters under the 1363 the bootloader passes (checked from captured lines at build). The init takes the slot from androidboot.slot_suffix, the device tree, bootconfig, then root=PARTUUID as a last resort; sources that disagree, or none, refuse; the log says which source gave it. dyndbg moves to a run-time write in the debug init.
why: Run 8: the bootloader cut our command line and the slot suffix with it, so the init refused. The Top Coordinator's additions of 2026-11-23 18:05 ask for exactly this order (fs_mgr) and no hardcoded slot.
rejected: Hardcoding the slot in the image: works in one slot only and hides the cause. root=PARTUUID as the only source: the booted slot only, and it hides a missing word. Keeping dyndbg on the command line: about 200 characters for a diagnostic the init can write later.

brief: The production stage 2 init is the root init plus the petters block and a hold script that ends them; no debug init with its word off; the kernel comes from the int/ tag
decision: build/initramfs-root-production/init = the root init byte for byte plus two PRODUCTION-BLOCKs: block 1 starts a petter on every watchdog device (supervisor, looks again each second) right after the modules and before the command line, slot, name or card; block 2 replaces the root's hold script by one that only counts and then ends the petters and resets the phone. No gadget, telnet, debug log or word. The image is built by build/build-ufs-root-production.sh TAG from a detached checkout of int/walleye/ufs-on/v7.3/N (build-ufs-root-image.sh with PRODUCTION_INIT=yes KERNEL_TAG=TAG; its checks stop the build).
why: Run 11 passed all 29 steps with the debug image, whose gadget and telnet are for finding out, not for staying (a passwordless root shell on a cable). The petters are the part run 7-11 needed; Android pets one non-secure WDT0 (research walleye-android-watchdog-read-fix). Same shape as the debug init keeps one proof (tests/host/ufs-root-production-init.sh: text equals the root init outside the blocks, petters before the slot and card, root init QEMU proof passes with it).
rejected: The debug init with walleye.debug left off: the gadget, telnet and log code would stay in the image that stays on the phone. A kernel built from a tree by hand: the tag is the one named, read-back kernel (walleye-next-image-from-an-int-tag). brief: Step 16 asserts governor userspace, set_freq 50 MHz read back and gear HS_GEAR1; cur_freq 50 or 100 MHz both pass (100 is core_clk's rounding), 200 MHz fails
decision: The pin stays 'userspace + set_freq 50000000' (max_freq 50000000 on a node without userspace). Step 16 asserts what holds the pin and the state it gives: governor reads userspace, userspace/set_freq reads 50000000 (or max_freq reads 50000000), power_info gear reads HS_GEAR1; cur_freq is printed and passes as 50000000 or 100000000 and fails at anything else. It captures and prints the full evidence named in the research (before/after the governor write and after set_freq, dmesg after the write, debugfs gcc_ufs_axi_clk clk_rate where present).
why: Research walleye-ufs-pin-100mhz-read: on v7.3 ufshcd_devfreq_target rounds the request through clk_round_rate(GCC_UFS_AXI_CLK), whose mainline table starts at 100 MHz, and returns early while clock scaling is idle-suspended, so cur_freq (devfreq's previous_freq) reads 100 MHz for a pin that is in force; the gear follows the scale-down state (min_gear HS-G1). Runs 6 and 7 refused a correct pin.
rejected: Asserting cur_freq == 50000000 (runs 6-7's check): false refusal at idle, cur_freq is bookkeeping, not the clock. Asserting min_freq: the QoS floor, unchanged by the write, proves nothing. Switching to the max_freq clamp only: the same target() and the same rounding, and it would leave simple_ondemand free to re-evaluate; no gain. Adding a 50 MHz entry to gcc-msm8998's ufs_axi_clk_src (Android has one) now: a kernel change before anything shows the 100 MHz core clock bears on the silence; kept as a question for the evidence. Holding low by clkscale_enable=0: scales UP on both trees (research walleye-ufs-hold-the-clock-read).
scope: google-walleye-lab: walleye-tries step 16 (the_clock_is_pinned_low), its builder and the phone keeper's next UFS run
